plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable), and I never overpay since the price is set by the second-highest bid, not my own. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (essentially a second-price auction mechanism), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my true value of $27 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, which guarantees non-negative profit whenever I win. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if I win; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding is optimal here.

Since this is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $13 to maximize expected profit.
